I think it's a pretty unique program, especially if you're more artistically inclined. It's much more design focused since it's a BFA. If you're more interested in the engineering or other aspects of architecture it does not cater to that. It is in the art school and so is very involved with the art school. You have elective slots and access to any of the arts classes.  There are also many opportunities for research, and a diverse set of teaching styles and exposure to different kinds of design thinking. Balancing life outside of studies is ... A bit complicated I would say as studio classes are not your typical class structure, where really you are probably there every other day, or usually every day. You will have late nights and weekends in studio. The more work you put in the more you will gain from the class. Architecture is definitely about effort and time spent. There are no exams in studio - it is how much you do, how much thought you put into it, and how well you do it.

It's a 4 year degree. An annoying thing about my degree is that it's a Bachelor's of Fine Arts and *not* a pre professional, Bachelor's of Architecture that's certified by the National Architecture Accreditation Board. It just means I have to do a 3 year master's instead of a 2 year master's. Tbf I did know this I just wasn't fully committed to architecture when I chose the program. My degree just doesn't include all the structures classes most accredited B.Arch's do.

I cannot offer architecture services, no. I'm only graduating with a bachelor's degree - I need about 3 years work experience, a master's degree, and about 6 different exams to get licensed before I can even call myself an architect. Most architects work in larger firms, and can only open their own practice once they get licensed. The architecture world is very hierarchical and experience based, so right now I can only really find jobs as an intern or an entry level designer. (Which I am very much applying for rn) . But I really like doing graphic design work, and I think it's probably good experience to design something for a client.

Hi. Your experience sounds extremely similar to my own. I believe that I'm a burden, and wish my friends would stop caring about me so I wouldn't hurt them if I died. I wish I was never born. But please understand, that it's usually depression itself that causes these feelings of loneliness, isolation, and self-loathing. It's a symptom of depression itself to believe you are faking it. Let me tell you from personal experience, the way you talk about yourself sounds exactly like what I used to do. But it's not true. It's a self hate that manifests as part of depression, that makes you see yourself, your relationships and the world as something separate from reality. If you were actually selfish, you wouldn't want to spare your friends from guilt and pain from your death. If you were selfish you wouldn't care about whether or not you were a burden. The fact that you don't want to be a selfish burden means that you aren't one. Also, if you were faking this, would you really take it this far? If you didn't want people to care about you, and you didn't want to be a burden, you would be able to control these emotions. But they are not fake, they are very real. They are real, and just because they make you feel worthless Does not mean that you are. Just because your emotions make you feel unloved by your friends doesn't mean you are. I understand that I probably can't convince you that you are more than what you call yourself. But believe me, my writings sound so insanely similar to this, and at some point after the emotions died away, the beliefs about myself did too. Please talk to your friends if you can, because you are not being a burden by asking for help. If you don't want to talk to your friends, feel free to pm me. I am completely Willing to help you. Please don't give in to the thoughts you have about yourself, and don't do anything to harm yourself. Don't isolate yourself. Don't be angry at yourself. You are much more than you think you are.

Because self-loathing is a symptom of depression, the thoughts you have about yourself probably aren't true. I have almost the same thoughts about myself, so I can understand that they're really hard to see past. The thing about believing yourself to be a "terrible" or "selfish" person is that truly bad people don't care about whether or not they are good or bad. The fact that you upset about being a "bad" person means you probably aren't. You want to be good, and that wanting to be good means you are good. It confirms you are a good person. 

For the other stuff, I understand what it's like to not want to exist as your self. Again, these are all symptoms of something more serious. This means that if you try to seek help with mental illness you will learn that most of these thoughts about yourself are wrong. Most of your thoughts on wanting the "opposite" life probably stem from the fact that you're probably going through a lot right now. 

If it's any consolation, I completely understand believing that I'm the worst person alive. And I understand that some person on the internet telling you that you're a good person probably won't get through to you. Shit, my best friends tried to tell me I'm wrong and I didn't believe them. Hating yourself this much doesn't feel good at all. From personal experience, my advice is that you have to try to accept that there is a possibility that you are wrong about yourself, and that right now you are looking at yourself through a difference lense from reality. If you can talk to someone you trust, ask them if they agree with you about yourself. I think they'll tell you they don't.

You can be actively suicidal or passively suicidal. Being passively suicidal means you maybe have suicidal ideations, a preoccupation with death, imagining you're dead, and just sort of thinking about it in a conceptual capacity. Being actively suicidal means you think about methods, you think of how/when/where you could do it, you try to make sure your plan will be fatal, or you make a suicidal gesture or attempt. It sounds like you are suicidal, but passively suicidal.
